doc.title: Jack Sheldon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Running a big band today
summary: Putting a big band together, young versatile players, the AT&T golf show, and Tom Kubis's charts.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: What’s it like to try to put a big band together these days?

Oh it’s a thrill. The musicians are so great. When I do it I just put the rhythm section — if I’ve got a good rhythm section, I’m happy then, because then nothing much can happen. These kids that you get are sensational. They can read anything, they all play lead and play jazz and do everything now. It’s a different world. I think now you have to do everything. You have to play lead, play jazz and play classical, play every which way. Because that’s what the studios want now. They don’t specialize like they used to.
Yeah you would get known as, you know, call this guy—

Yeah I was always a jazz player. And now everybody has to do everything. But to put a big band together, it’s always a thrill. We just got through working the AT&T Golf Tournament up there with Clint Eastwood, and we had a great show. Diana Krall and Glen Campbell and Michael Bolton, and Clint Eastwood and his wife and my band, and oh it was sensational.
Who writes most of your charts?
Tom Kubis. I don’t know if you know him. He’s a young guy. He teaches at Golden West College, a real genius. Great composer.
